A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KFD/FPL/LVLM framework and retain identifiable equations, experiments and figures. All supplied material supports comparison, including v1's template-only appendix and v2's substantive Appendix A.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original detection results, localization examples and experiments varying training data, prompt-tuning components and LLM architectures.

after.justification: The retained original experiments are supplemented by DF40 results, reference-optimization ablations, perturbation tests, inference timings and qualitative dialogue and failure examples.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Figure 3 revise the documented text-conditioning procedure: v1 places learnable context before the text encoder, whereas v2 concatenates learnable embeddings with encoded description features. The overall KFD–FPL–LLM pipeline and losses remain unchanged. LoRA was already used in v1's ablation experiments.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on 15 DF40 manipulation methods spanning face swapping, reenactment and entire-face synthesis, including GAN and diffusion generators. Appendix A.2 also introduces six corrupted FF++ input scenarios. These substantially extend the manipulation and input-condition coverage beyond v1's retained datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CFM, ED, ProDet, RepDFD and UDD. The corresponding LVLM comparison also adds RepDFD and UDD, substantially broadening the competitive comparison. V1's P-Tuning row becomes Clipping with the same cited work and scores; this is a rename rather than an additional baseline.

E3.justification: Added evaluation designs include controlled training with and without reference optimization, six FF++ perturbation conditions, and per-frame inference timing on one RTX 4090. Existing main training settings remain unchanged. The 500-step budget for low-data experiments and 32-frame LLM aggregation are newly specified; the PDFs do not establish that these disclosures represent changed earlier procedures.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of reference optimization in Table 8, corruption robustness in Table 9, and failure cases where correct localization accompanies incorrect LLM judgments in Figure 6. It also supplies previously absent multi-turn conversation examples. The prompt-tuning, training-dataset and LLM-architecture ablations are retained, while the low-data analysis is revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original KFD scores, but added baselines change rankings: its DFDC AUC of 79.12 is now below UDD's 81.21. FAK-Owl's CDF2 AUC changes from 73.51 to 60.85 between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3. The low-data table has replaced values and dataset columns, with a newly disclosed budget. DF40, robustness, reference-ablation, timing and qualitative results are also added.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same similarity calculations, losses and image-blending formulation. Renaming consistency maps from C to rho does not change the mathematics. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that knowledge-guided visual-text alignment and forgery prompts enable generalizable, explainable detection with multi-turn dialogue. The rewritten abstract and added DF40 evidence preserve these core contributions and the broad superiority claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly attributes detection failures to the mismatch between general VQA training and localized forgery reasoning, acknowledging that accurate localization can coexist with wrong textual judgments. Appendix A.3 also discusses increased inference cost relative to CADDM and FAK-Owl. These introduce substantive qualifications to v1's largely unqualified accuracy and explainability narrative.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies description strings and their GPT-4/human-validation provenance, batch sizes, LoRA target modules, rank, alpha and dropout, plus frame sampling, response parsing and video-score aggregation. V2 also specifies the localization-loss weight and low-data training budget. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's backbone, optimizer, hardware and epoch details.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for recent comparison methods, ImageBind, DF40 and GenFace, while removing several background citations with the revised introduction. The related-work discussion and positioning around external knowledge and fine-grained forgery prompts remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory motivation are revised around LVLM–forensics misalignment, terminology and comparison prose are clarified, and publication details and acknowledgements are added. The placeholder appendix becomes organized subsections. The main section sequence and much of the existing method and analysis prose are retained.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework and KFD diagrams, removes the standalone FPL architecture diagram and detailed detector-branch schematics, enlarges the retained GradCAM display, and expands localization panels. It restructures the LVLM comparison into classifier/VQA blocks and adds experimental tables, failure illustrations and extensive dialogue screenshots.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves important deficiencies in v1's evidence and reproducibility: the placeholder appendix becomes substantive implementation documentation and actual dialogue examples, while new component and robustness tests strengthen validation. Explicit failure analysis also qualifies the explainability claim. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including Table 10's CDF2 label with CDF1-matching AUC values and superiority language broader than the expanded Table 1 supports.
